description:
Found by cold review of fz-5xp.15. All three doors agree with each other and
differ from Elixir.

    dbg(:"")          fz  :atom_3      elixir  :""
    dbg(:"foo bar")   fz  :foo bar     elixir  :"foo bar"

`any_value::debug::render_atom` prints the name bare, and for an EMPTY name
falls through to a synthesised `:atom_N` placeholder. Elixir quotes any atom
whose name is not a bare identifier, and prints an empty atom as `:""`.

MATTERS FOR THE ORACLE: an oracle twin printing such an atom diverges, so
fixtures currently have to avoid them. `behavior/to_string` says so explicitly
rather than depending on it.

Note the placeholder is a SECOND answer to "what is this atom called" -- the
other is `fz_atom_to_binary`, which consults the table and panics if the name
is missing. They agreed only by luck; the empty-name case is where they
visibly disagreed, one printing `:atom_3` and the other aborting until the AOT
table bug behind it was fixed. Fold them.

DONE = `dbg` quotes an atom exactly when Elixir does, with a fixture covering
empty, spaced, punctuation, unicode and ordinary names, and one implementation
of the name lookup.
title: dbg does not quote atoms that need quoting
